extracted.intended_audience: R package authors/developers submitting packages to rOpenSci (or preparing packages for peer review/CRAN/Bioconductor)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for developing, documenting, testing, and preparing an R package for rOpenSci software peer review (and general CRAN/Bioconductor readiness). Covers naming, API design, documentation, testing, CI, licensing, authorship, and related best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package name and metadata — Naming your package
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly recommend short, descriptive names in lower case. If your package deals with one or more commercial services, please make sure the name does not violate branding guidelines. Do not choose a package name that's already used on CRAN or Bioconductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check name availability and offensiveness (e.g. pak::pkg_name_check(), search engines). Balance uniqueness (easier tracking/search) vs discoverability (name close to topic). Avoid offensive terms in other languages. See linked blog posts for deeper discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforms — cross-platform support
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should run on all major platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowed for packages that interact with system-specific functions or wrap utilities limited to certain platforms, but authors should make every effort for cross-platform compatibility, including system-specific compilation or containerization of external utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package API — function and argument naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions and arguments naming should form a common, logical programming API that is easy to read and to auto-complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer object_verb() naming (object = data/API, verb = action). For functions that manipulate and return same-type objects, make the object/data the first argument to enhance pipe compatibility. Strongly recommend snake_case. Avoid name conflicts with base or popular packages (ggplot2, dplyr, magrittr, data.table). Keep argument naming and order consistent across similar functions. Package functions importing data must return objects, not assign to the global environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Console messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cli or base R message()/warning() to communicate; avoid print() or cat() except for print.*()/str.*() methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a way for users to opt out of verbosity at the package level (environment variable or option), ideally with multiple verbosity levels (e.g., none/inform/debug) rather than a logical flag. Respect NO_COLOR convention. Consider translations for messages (potools). Avoid print()/cat() because they are harder for users to suppress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive/Graphical Interfaces — reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing a GUI (e.g., Shiny), include a mechanism to automatically reproduce steps taken in the GUI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include auto-generation of code to reproduce outcomes, output of intermediate values, or clear/documented mapping between GUI actions and scripted functions. See examples (tabulizer, shiny apps that do code generation). Test GUIs (see Testing section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Input checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a consistent method for checking inputs across the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can use base R checks, an R package, or custom helpers — consistency is the key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages wrapping web resources (API clients)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your package accesses a web API or another web resource, follow specific practices to be a good API client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requests send a user agent and allow users to override it; consider different user agents on CI vs development. Document defaults and any choices. Help users by handling pagination and rate limiting. Reproduce API errors and explain them with informative messages. Consider exporting both high-level convenience functions and low-level endpoint functions for advanced control (e.g., gh::gh()). Refer to linked blog post for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages wrapping external software
rubrics_metrics.description: Document clearly how to install any required external software or libraries and provide helpers where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit steps for common operating systems, provide a 'sitrep' function checking installation status with helpful hints, and if possible a helper function to aid installation (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code style and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a consistent code style for package R/ scripts and functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended resources: The R Packages book, tidyverse style guide. Use tools like styler or Air and lintr. You may choose = or <- for assignment but be consistent; avoid ->. Note R6 requires = inside class construction. Use lintr to identify improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITATION file
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should have a CITATION file; CRAN requires CITATION files to be declared as bibentry items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create with usethis::use_citation(), populate via citation(). If archiving releases on Zenodo, add concept DOI to CITATION. If publishing a software paper after review, add it to the CITATION file. Consider CITATION.cff with cffr package and keep it up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: README presence and content
rubrics_metrics.description: All packages should have README.md in the repository root with structured content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: README should include: package name, CI/test coverage badges and rOpenSci badge (once review starts), short description (what/why), links to vignettes, installation instructions (remotes/pak/R-universe), setup notes (auth tokens), brief demo, comparisons to similar packages, citation information, and repostatus badge if used. Consider README.Rmd to combine text and runnable demo code, and keep extensive examples in vignettes. Add code of conduct and contribution guidelines. After submission add the rOpenSci peer-review badge with the correct issue_id. Organize many badges in an HTML table to make info accessible. If package wraps a data/service, README should describe that resource and link to relevant docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation — general
rubrics_metrics.description: All exported functions should be fully documented with examples, and the package should have top-level documentation and at least one substantial HTML vignette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vignettes should illustrate realistic use cases and present examples progressing from basic to advanced. Provide package-level docs (?foobar or ?`foobar-package`). Documentation and vignettes should provide multiple points of entry and outline prerequisite knowledge. Include citations where appropriate. If accessing a data source, DESCRIPTION must identify the organization responsible and include a URL to a public-facing page about the data. Avoid unnecessary startup messages in favor of documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: roxygen2 use
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci requests all submissions use roxygen2 for documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use roxygen2 tags and support for Markdown. Document return types under @return. Clearly indicate default parameter values in documentation. Use @family to group functions; use @examples, @example <path>, and @exampleIf for examples storage/conditional runs. Use #' @keywords internal or #' noRd as appropriate. roxygen2 supports R6 classes (>=7.0.0). Reuse doc pieces across README/vignettes where useful. Note: multilingual manual pages not yet supported out-of-the-box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: When including example datasets, ensure proper redistribution and attribution and that the data comply with rOpenSci's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use base R datasets like penguins, or redistribute documented data with proper attribution; avoid data that is hurtful or alienating.

rubrics_metrics.name: URLs in documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: CRAN checks URLs and does not allow redirects such as 301.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use urlchecker to find redirects and replace URLs with their final targets. Escaping URLs to avoid CRAN checks may break clickability and requires you to implement URL checking to avoid broken links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation website (pkgdown) and deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a documentation website for your package (pkgdown recommended) and set up automatic deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before approval/transfer, manage automatic deployment yourself (e.g., pkgdown or tic); after transfer rOpenSci will build pkgdown for you with a template (rotemplate). If vignettes need credentials, precompute or cache responses since docs server can't use credentials. Update website URLs after transfer. Central builds are monitored at dev.ropensci.org and bugs reported to ropensci/docs or rotemplate repo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation website localization
rubrics_metrics.description: If documentation is written in a language other than English and supported by rOpenSci, declare that language for pkgdown localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multilingual pkgdown sites are not yet available out-of-the-box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping functions in the reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Group related functions in the reference using roxygen2 and pkgdown features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @family tags (roxygen2 >=6.1.1) to create 'See also' links and enable pkgdown's has_concept grouping. To customize cross-reference text, provide rd_family_title in man/roxygen/meta.R. See examples in drake and optiRum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding of authors on pkgdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can be branded on the pkgdown site with clickable names or logos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add author URLs or replace names with logos via pkgdown/usethis configuration if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navbar and site navigation tweaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Tweak the pkgdown navbar to improve navigability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the main vignette 'pkg-name.Rmd' yields a 'Get started' navbar link. Refer to pkgdown docs for navbar configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math rendering on pkgdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow pkgdown documentation for math rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci template is compatible with pkgdown's math rendering configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a package logo if desired (usethis::use_logo()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no logo is provided, rOpenSci docs builder will use the rOpenSci logo instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship metadata (Authors@R)
rubrics_metrics.description: DESCRIPTION should list authors and contributors using Authors@R syntax with roles; include ORCID for persons and ROR for organizations if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Writing R Extensions for details. If reviewers made substantial contributions and consent, list them with role 'rev' and include a comment linking to the review issue. Do not list editors as contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship of included code and copyright clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: When including code from other sources, ownership of copyright and IP must be clear and unambiguous, preserving copyright/license statements and correct authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CRAN Repository Policy. Prefer Authors@R with 'ctb' roles for authors of included code or use 'cph' roles for copyright holders. Respect trademarks. See examples for how to annotate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence
rubrics_metrics.description: The package must have a CRAN- or OSI-accepted license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See R Packages book for license selection. If bundling code from other sources, acknowledge original authors in DESCRIPTION (role = 'cph' where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing — R CMD check and unit tests
rubrics_metrics.description: All packages should pass R CMD check (devtools::check()) on all major platforms and include a test suite covering major functionality and error behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for test coverage ≥75% (lower coverage will require explanation). Use testthat (or tinytest) and write tests as you write functions. Tests should be easy to understand and self-contained; avoid code outside test_that() blocks. For Shiny apps use shinytest2/shinytest. For plot tests use vdiffr. Use HTTP-testing tools (httptest2, httptest, vcr, webfakes) for packages interacting with web resources. Use skip_on_cran() for API tests likely to fail on CRAN, and skip_if_offline() where appropriate. Use CI and coverage reports to identify untested lines. Run tests locally before submission (Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN='true') may help).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples (documentation examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include extensive examples in documentation to demonstrate usage and help catch regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples not wrapped in \dontrun{} or \donttest{} will be executed by R CMD check. For examples requiring authentication or long runs, wrap appropriately (\dontrun{}, try(), or use @exampleIf). Run examples on CI; configure CI to run dontrun/donttest if needed with R CMD check args. Use devtools::run_examples() to run examples locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package dependencies — minimize and manage
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor fewer dependencies and manage them consciously to reduce maintenance and installation burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh benefits of dependency functionality vs maintenance cost. Options include copying small stable functions (with attribution) instead of adding heavy deps; import functions from the package that defines them (not from one that re-exports them); prefer Imports over Depends; list test/doc packages in Suggests; explicitly state minimum versions when necessary; re-export individual functions rather than Depends when exposing dependency functions; check development status of dependencies; handle Bioconductor dependencies with clear install instructions. For system dependencies, indicate in DESCRIPTION, check sysreqsdb, consider configure scripts, and provide helpful error messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended scaffolding and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recommended, modern packages for common tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTTP clients: httr2/httr/curl/crul preferred over RCurl. JSON: jsonlite. XML: xml2. Spatial: prefer sf; rgdal/maptools/rgeos retired. Refer to r-spatial community guidance and linked migration notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version control (Git)
rubrics_metrics.description: Package source files must be tracked with Git.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensible branch naming (default branch should not be 'master'; prefer 'main'). Use .gitignore for junk files (.DS_Store). Tools: gert, usethis Git/GitHub helpers, usethis::git_vaccinate(), gitignore package. Follow later git workflow tips in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous CRAN gotchas
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid common CRAN submission pitfalls in Title/Description, examples, and R build infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title must be in Title Case and not end with a period. Do not include 'in R' or 'with R' in Title. Avoid starting Description with the package name or 'This package ...'. Include links in Description (enclosed in angle brackets). Quote package names/external software in Title/Description with single quotes. Avoid long-running tests/examples (use testthat::skip_on_cran). Include top-level files and CI config in .Rbuildignore. See ThinkR 'Prepare for CRAN' checklist for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRAN checks monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Once on CRAN, packages are regularly checked on different platforms and failures may prompt CRAN contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor CRAN check state via foghorn package and CRAN checks badges. React to non-false-positive failures promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioconductor gotchas
rubrics_metrics.description: If targeting Bioconductor, follow Bioconductor packaging guidelines and updated developer book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Bioconductor resources for submission and development specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further guidance and community processes
rubrics_metrics.description: For rOpenSci submissions use the software-review repo and direct additional questions to the rOpenSci team; read authors guide and collaboration guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the issue tracker for questions, incorporate advice from Collaboration Guide, and consult provided books, tutorials, blogs, and MOOCs for learning package development.
